rv.q: NEW YORK — Patrick Stewart's suave performance in the Chichester Festival Theatre production of "Macbeth," which opened Tuesday at the Lyceum Theatre on Broadway, can be scored a triumph, but it comes with a few provisos.
Stewart unquestionably succeeds, while the rest of this Macbeth more visibly boils in the toil and trouble of finding itself.

cn.t: Patrick Stewart delivers a triumph in the title role, though the production comes with reservations. Critics praise the lead performance while noting the Scottish play's notorious difficulty.

vs.sum: The Lyceum Theatre offers good sightlines and a charming Beaux Arts ambiance, but suffers from cramped seating and small restrooms. Ideal for intimate dramas, but patrons should be prepared for less comfort during their visit.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No elevator. Infrared devices available.
